messages:
Alex: Hey team — getting 400 on a tool call that works locally. Error in logs says schema validation failed (unexpected control char). Sending sample. :eyes:
Maria: can you paste the exact payload you sent (raw) and the curl you used?
Alex: here's the payload I see in the client (copied exactly):
```json
{"path":"C:\\temp\\file.txt", "notes":"check color:\\u001b[31mred\\u001b[0m", "items":["one", "two",], "meta":"contains\\u0000null"}
```
Alex: curl I used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"path":"C:\\temp\\file.txt","notes":"check color:\\u001b[31mred\\u001b[0m","items":["one","two",],"meta":"\\x00"}'`
Maria: ah — two obvious problems: trailing comma in `items` and an embedded NUL/escape. Also your shell is expanding $TOKEN because you used single quotes incorrectly in some shells.
Jordan: also that `\u001b` (ANSI ESC) is valid JSON, but some clients translate `\x00` into a literal NUL which many servers reject. Schema validator throws on control chars.
Maria: can you repro with `--data-binary` and pass a file instead of inlining? that avoids shell quoting issues. Example: `cat payload.json | curl -X POST ... --data-binary @-`
Alex: tried that, still failed. Server log shows: `schema_validator: invalid escape at pos 72` then `400 malformed_tool_args`.
Jordan: @Alex can you attach the exact bytes (hexdump) of the body your client sends? sometimes UTF-8 vs latin1 gets messy.
Alex: uploaded hexdump: `3c 7b 22 70 61 74 68 22 3a 22 43 3a 5c 5c 74 65 6d 70 5c 5c 66 69 6c 65 2e 74 78 74 22 2c 22 6e 6f 74 65 73 22 3a 22 63 68 65 63 6b 20 63 6f 6c 6f 72 3a 1b 5b 33 31 6d 72 65 64 1b 5b 30 6d 22 2c 22 69 74 65 6d 73 22 3a 5b 22 6f 6e 65 22 2c 22 74 77 6f 22 2c 5d 2c 22 6d 65 74 61 22 3a 22 00 22 7d`
Maria: confirmed there's an actual 0x00 byte inside payload, and a trailing 0x2c before the closing bracket (the trailing comma). That combination trips our parser (we treat NUL as unallowed control char).
Alex: original client lib is node 14 with `request` wrapper, it probably turned `\x00` into a literal byte.
Jordan: workaround: strip control chars before sending or base64-encode metadata if it can contain binary. Also remove trailing commas (some JS serializers do that if manually concatenated).
Maria: for customers hitting this, we should: 1) return a clearer error code and message mentioning NUL and trailing comma, 2) add a short doc note showing how to send binary in `meta` (base64 + content-type), 3) add a quick detection rule in the intake parser to reject with friendly message instead of a generic schema failure.
Sam: setting priority P2; escalating to eng-runtime. @Jordan can you take a look and propose a parser-side improvement?
Jordan: will do, starting with a small sniff for 0x00 and trailing commas in arrays/objects; also add a link to docs in the error.
SupportBot: Ticket #S-2026 created and assigned to eng-runtime.
Alex: thanks — will try base64 and confirm. :thumbsup:
